ClientResponses.Response:
Hello! Due to the small size of the grill, the location and shape of the burner, and the heat retaining properties of the porcelain enameled cast iron grates, it may be challenging to obtain a low temperature on the Q 1200. 
To obtain a lower than 420 degrees temperature, you may want to preheat the grill on Low, instead of High, as we usually advise. 
You may also want to use a foil pan and a grilling pan to block some of the heat emanating from the burner. Lastly, do make sure your grill is clean, since grease will generate extra heat. Do make sure to scrape out any debris that builds up in the cookbox, and also empty out the drip pan as needed. We hope these tips help. Thanks!
ClientResponses.Name: Weber Grills

Results.ReviewText: Regardless of how the grill is started up by preheating or not or by what temperature it is started, it will not go below 420 degrees even on low. Weber sent me a new valve and regulator which I installed, but it made no difference. There are some foods that I like to cook low and slow. The two representatives that I spoke to seemed to think that it should cook at a lower heat and that it could take some time to do that. In fact the manual states that it will run hotter initially. The grill seems well made and cooks steaks, etc, but I want a lower heat. If it never will cook lower I would have chosen a different brand. I have a full size NG grill that I have enjoyed for 25 years and it is a quality product. This is a grill that I take RVing. It makes no difference whether I use a one pound cannister or a 20 pound tank with adapter. I am disappointed.

Results.ReviewText:
My Q 1200 is the third Webber I currently own (22" Kettle, and Spirit).  It was purchased to replace the grill that came with our newly purchased 2004 travel trailer.  I originally ordered a Coleman Roadtrip 285 since I was concerned about a larger cooking area.  Luckily the Coleman it was delayed, and I discovered the City Escape Griller YouTube Channel.  I came to my senses and purchased the Q 1200.  I couldn't be happier with the decision.  
I used the 1lb tank until my adapters arrived allowing me to connect directly to my trailer's quick connect auxiliary port.  By removing the Q's regulator, I can connect to the trailer's already regulated tanks with a 20ft hose.  I attached a quick connect to the existing Q regulator so I can use the 1lb tanks if the hose does not reach, or if I use the Q away from my trailer.
The Q is typical Webber quality, and cooking constancy.  I've considered firing it up at home just to learn more about its capabilities.
Results.Title: There's No Question About the Q

Results.ReviewText: Works very well to take along with us in the pop-up camper, but makes a mess with grease splatter. I like this grill mostly due to the fact it gets hot, sears well, cooks relatively evenly, is compact and is designed so I can secure it to the camper with a cable lock. The only complaints I have are that the grease splatter isn’t contained really at all due to the very low sidewalls around the grill grate plates and also, tool hooks molded into the fold out tray tables would be a nice touch.
Results.Title: Compact, convenient but messy.

Results.ReviewText: Our motor home is one of the smaller Sprinter based ones. This grill was purchased to go in our newly acquired motor home.It barely fits in the outside storage bin. I am so glad it does, because we love this thing. I got the half griddle piece to make it more adaptable for cooking pancakes and such. Works like a charm. Most importantly, my husband says he is glad I picked this grill.  I reviewed the heck out of all the choices I could find and came back to this grill. Starts with the push of a button, heats quickly, has a thermometer on the hood, has a removable catch tray for the drippings, and cleans up easily. The side tables fold up and into the grill for compact storage. We use grill mats on our grill, food comes out great and a couple papers towels clean it up. We got the hose to attach to a larger propane bottle, but so far the one pound size lasts about three meals for us depending on what is being cooked. Seems very durable and should last us for years to come.
Results.Title: My husband does the cooking and likes this

Results.ReviewText: Love it! This grill is a dependable work-horse. We do A LOT of grilling.  The footprint of the grill is not large at all, but the cooking surface more than meets the needs of two people, and then some.  It easily fits 4-5 burgers and 4-5 brats in a single shot. It's very easy to control the temperature and I have yet to find a "hot spot".  It cooks evenly -- we've cooked corn on the cob, pork steaks, chops, chicken, kebabs, you name it.  We are VERY satisfied with this grill and highly recommend it.  The only modification we made was to purchase an adapter that allowed us to hook up a standard sized propane tank to it.  We had the same model years ago that we loved that got stolen off of our patio.  For some idiotic reason we replaced it with a larger Kitchenaid model we bought at one of the big box stores.  What a mistake!  The Kitchenaid model had hot and cold spots and there was no controlling the temperature.  It was either 0 or 600 degrees.  Ridiculous considering the money we paid for it.  We got so fed up, we went back to this little baby and haven't looked back.  Thanks Weber!  And thanks for the excellent customer service as far as the shipping and packing (we purchased the grill on the Weber website).  A very positive experience, overall.
